comments.author: Jemmeh
comments.story_title: Ask HN: How are some people exceptionally productive?
comments.why_zh: 该演讲很有说服力地讨论了休息和高效学习。
comments.quote_zh: Study Less, Study Smart 是 Marty Lobdell 的一场演讲，其中很有说服力地讨论了这一点。
comments.text_zh: 1.) 把事情写下来。组织好。Google Calendar 和 Trello 意味着我绝不会忘记做任何事，也不会把脑力花在记住所有事情上。这通过让我更放松来帮助平衡。晚上我不会担心明天要做的所有事情，而这会让很多人睡得更少。我会说：“它在我的清单上，我明天会处理。”我睡得像个婴儿。我把事情做完了。2.) 如果你在寻找平衡，照顾好你的身体。1 小时锻炼只占你一天的 4%。为它腾出时间，做一些你喜欢的有活力的活动。（即使那是玩一小时 DDR。）提前批量做健康的饭菜。生病和死亡可没有生产力。3.) 休息。当你感觉思绪游移，过去 5 分钟读的东西什么都记不住时，就该短暂休息一下了。花 5 分钟，绕着楼走一圈，然后再坐回来。你可能觉得自己继续坐在那里工作会高效得多，但如果你是在原地打转，甚至把事情弄得更糟，那你就没有高效。Study Less, Study Smart 是 Marty Lobdell 的一场演讲，其中很有说服力地讨论了这一点。[VIDEO] 4.) 专注。移除干扰。关掉所有你工作不需要的窗口。关上办公室门，每小时只查一次邮件。无论你需要做什么来专注，就去做。
comments.text: 1.) Write things down. Get organized. Google Calendar and Trello mean I never forget to do anything and I don't exercise brain power on remembering it all. This helps balance by being more relaxed. At night I don't worry about all the things I have to do tomorrow, which makes a lot of people sleep less. I say, "It's on my list, which I will tackle tomorrow." I sleep like a baby. I get things done. 2.) If you're looking for balance, take care of your body. 1 hour workout is 4% of your day. Make time for it, and do something active that you enjoy. (Even if that's playing DDR for an hour). Cook healthy meals in bulk ahead of time. Sick and dead isn't productive. 3.) Take breaks. When you feel your mind wandering, and you can't remember anything you've read in the past 5 minutes it's time to take a short break. Take 5 minutes, walk around the building, then sit back down. You might think you'll be so much more productive continuing to sit there working, but if you're working in circles or even making things worse, you are not being productive. Study Less, Study Smart is a talk by Marty Lobdell that eloquently discusses this. [VIDEO] 4.) Focus. Remove distractions. Close all the windows you don't need to work. Close your office door, answer your emails only once an hour. Whatever you need to do to focus.

comments.author: Jemmeh
comments.story_title: Ways to maximize your cognitive potential
comments.why_zh: 关于专注和有效工作的相关演讲
comments.text_zh: 作为一个难以集中注意力的人——A.) 尽量减少工作区域的视觉刺激。把桌上的东西都清走，把脸塞到角落里。（我把桌子转过去，背对走廊。）B.) 工作时记笔记。我会写 15 分钟代码，记下我正在做什么，然后（刻意地）分心一两分钟。等我回到工作时，我可以看看笔记，知道刚才在做什么，并从停下的地方继续。这真的能最大程度减少分心对我工作的影响。如果你想的话，可以从更短的“高效”时间段开始。练习专注能帮助你逐步延长能专注的时间。Youtube 上的相关演讲：[VIDEO]
comments.text: As a person who has trouble focusing-- A.) Minimize visual stimuli in your work area. Get everything off your desk, and shove your face in a corner. (I've turned my desk to face away from the hallway.) B.) Take notes as you work. I will write 15 minutes of code, take a note on what I'm doing, then get (purposefully) distracted for a minute or two. When I come back to my work, I can look at my note to see what I was doing and pick back up where I left off. It really minimizes the impact of distraction on my work. You can start out with lower chunks of "productive" time if you want. Practicing focus helps you to build up amount of time you can focus. Relevant talk on Youtube: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 这提出了些很好的观点，Martin Lombell 也在一场颇为经典、引人入胜的一小时讲座中讲过非常类似的内容：[VIDEO] 我在研究学习心理学时发现或挖掘到的其他一些“钻石”有：- 那些在计划中先安排娱乐和锻炼、再学习的学生，成绩比那些一开始就决定何时学习的学生更好；- 我们大多数人都能通过令人困惑、能揭示误解的内容学得更好，而不是简单内容——我们都假设得太多，就像 Veritasium 讲过的：[LINK] - 原则上，以不偷懒的媒介（也就是说，你需要能获得反馈，比如测验、重写或辅导）提供多样化内容所带来的“合意困难”，是建立可行的长期学习的关键方式；其他一些效应，比如 Spaced Repetition，只有在你能够坚持学习动机时才有好处，所以你确实需要优先考虑动机。文章提到学习风格未被证实；事实上，可以论证反过来才是真的：以混合、多样内容学习的人表现最好。但我们也喜欢对自己来说舒适的学习类型；这会提升动机。问题在于，横跨整个学期和多门课程来研究学生的情况很少发生，而那些关注在 10 分钟窗口内改变学习内容如何影响学生学到多少的研究，既不能复制熟悉某种学习内容风格的价值，也不能复制其成本

comments.text_zh: 我合作过的一些老师会这么做；也有一些很棒的老师（讲师），比如 Martin，会教有效的学习技巧：[VIDEO] 闪卡和 Anki 对我来说极其有效。我正在做一个学习工具，能从讲座幻灯片自动生成这些闪卡。除此之外，它还应用了其他学习心理学技巧——把内容拆成可管理的块，让你能看到自己的进度（增强你对考试覆盖范围的信心），还有一个类似考试环境的模式：先给你看相关幻灯片，然后向你提问，并要求你自由回忆，把记得的一切一股脑写到空白页上。之后它能对你的学习状况给出 realistic 的判断；这种通过主动自由回忆来学习的方式虽然更 intense，但长期来看最终比阅读、观看或测验都更有效。其他闪卡应用——甚至 Anki——忽略的一点是，学生必须有动力。他们在学习时必须享受、有视觉上的投入，并且有信心。他们在朝着目标积累知识时，必须觉得自己走在一条可持续、现实的路上。而且他们不必每天都学习才能做到这一点——他们只需要真正学到东西，并能看到自己的进度状态……我很兴奋现在在做 EdTech[Revision.ai]，它能揭示并检测误解，帮助学生消除它们。误解是一个巨大的机会——不亚于间隔重复
comments.text: Some of the teachers I have worked with do this; and there are some great teachers(lecturers) like Martin who teach effective studying techniques: [VIDEO] Flashcards and Anki were incredibly effective for me. I am building a study tool which automatically generates them from lecture slides. Beyond that, it applies other psychology of learning techniques - It breaks up content into manageable chunks you can see your progress on (to boost your confidence of exam coverage) and has an exam-conditions like mode where it shows you relevant slides, then asks you questions and to freely recall by blurting onto a blank page everything you remember. It's then able to give you a realistic judgement of your learning and this way of learning by actively recalling freely is, though more intense, ultimately more effective than either reading, watching or quizzing in the long term. The part of learning that other flashcard apps miss, even Anki, is that students must be motivated. They must enjoy, visually engage, and be confident as they study. They must feel they are on a sustainable realistic path as they gather knowledge when on the way to their goals. And they don't have to study every day to do that - they just need to genuinely learn and be able to see the state of their progress... I am excited to be working on EdTech now[Revision.ai] which unveils and detects misconceptions to aid the student in eliminating them. Misconceptions are a massive opportunity - as much as spaced repetition

comments.author: rramadass
comments.story_title: Book list for streetfighting computer scientists (2022)
comments.text_zh: 1）仔细阅读目录（ToC），了解每一章讲什么。分辨哪些章/节讲的是“概念/思想”，哪些讲的是“实现/技术”。2）阅读书的前言/序言/导论，作者通常会在那里给出阅读本书的行动计划。这会让你了解各章之间的依赖关系以及哪些章最重要，从而决定你的行动路径。3）如果书有附录/导论章节，梳理了所需的数学等背景知识复习，先读这些。4）按顺序过一遍每一章开头的导论部分和结尾的总结部分，所有章节都这样做。现在你虽然还有很多不清楚的地方，但已经对每章讲什么（动机和总结）有了概念。根据需要标记/划线/批注关键点和术语。5）现在，根据（1）和（2），你已经有了一组处理基本“概念/思想”的章/节，这就是你现在要按顺序开始学习的内容。手边备好纸笔，以便在文本上标记/划线/批注，并按需做笔记。你可以使用“SQ3R”（[LINK]）和“Cornell Note-taking method”（[LINK]）作为技巧。6）再过一遍（5）的内容，更好地掌握“概念/思想”。对于难以理解的主题，这可能还不够。记下原因；也许你仍然缺乏一些所需的背景知识/数学，需要补一补。确保不要过度深入支线；有时可以把它当作一个
comments.text: 1) Read the ToC carefully to see what each chapter is about. Identify which chapters/sections are about "Concepts/Ideas" vs. "Implementation/Technology". 2) Read the book's Foreward/Preface/Introduction where the author(s) often lay out a plan of action for reading the book. This will give you the dependencies among the chapters and which are the most important so that you can decide on your path of action. 3) If the book has appendices/introductory chapter which lays out some needed background knowledge refresher in Mathematics/etc. read these first. 4) Go through each chapter's beginning introductory section and last summary section in sequence for all the chapters. Now you have an idea of what each chapter is about (motivation and summary) even though much is still unknown.
